topics.title: Researchers outline more efficient path to fusion ignition
topics.summary: Scientists at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory have reported a potentially more efficient route to achieving fusion ignition. Their approach reverses the traditional sequence by heating plasma first and then increasing its density, which they say could bring practical fusion energy closer to reality.
topics.detail: The study, reported by Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, describes a new pathway to fusion ignition that departs from conventional schemes where density is typically raised before heating. The researchers propose that heating the plasma initially, followed by compression to higher density, may lower the overall energy required for ignition. They argue this route could reduce technical demands on future fusion facilities and accelerate efforts to develop fusion as an energy source, though further validation and experiments are still needed.

topics.title: MMX Mars moon mission scheduled for October launch
topics.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is scheduled to launch on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center on 20 October 2026 Japan time. The mission aims to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and return it to Earth, a first for any space mission.
topics.detail: According to the European Space Agency, MMX will lift off at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026, corresponding to the evening of 19 October in Europe. The spacecraft is expected to enter orbit around Mars in August 2027 and then begin orbiting Phobos from September 2027. During its operations around Phobos, MMX will collect samples from the moon’s surface for return to Earth. The mission is designed to improve understanding of Mars’s moons and their origin by directly analyzing material from Phobos in terrestrial laboratories.

topics.title: Perseverance sets new off-world driving distance record
topics.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has driven farther than any vehicle has on the surface of another world. On 11 October 2026, its odometer reached 28.10 miles, surpassing the previous record of 28.06 miles held by the Opportunity rover.
topics.detail: NASA reports that Perseverance reached 45.22 kilometers of total driving on Mars, slightly exceeding the 45.16 kilometers achieved by Opportunity during its mission from 2004 to 2018. The new record reflects the sustained mobility of Perseverance as it continues its exploration of Jezero Crater. The rover’s traverses support its ongoing science program, which includes studying rocks and sediments and collecting samples for possible future return to Earth.

topics.title: Event examines deep-sea mining plans and controversies
topics.summary: A presentation titled "Deep-Sea Mining in Norway and Beyond" is scheduled at Umeå University on 16 October 2026. It explores how deep-sea mining is being promoted for critical minerals and how these plans are contested in different political and cultural contexts.
topics.detail: The event description notes that deep-sea mining is increasingly framed as a way to secure minerals for the green transition by extending extraction thousands of meters below the ocean surface. The presentation draws on ethnographic research conducted since late 2023 to examine developments in Norway’s mining plans, United States ambitions to secure seabed minerals, and opposition in American Samoa. It highlights tensions among geopolitical competition, scientific uncertainty about deep-ocean ecosystems, and ancestral relations to the deep sea reported by affected communities.
